title: Preserve watch fired-registry TTL under LRU access
summary: Expire every fired-registry entry whose fixed TTL has elapsed, independent of the LRU access order used for the bounded registry cap.
reason: Remediate P3 AUDIT-FIND-W01-027. Accessing an older fired entry moved it behind newer entries, where first-unexpired short-circuiting could suppress it indefinitely past the configured TTL.
behavior_before: Expiration stopped at the first unexpired OrderedDict entry even though has_fired reordered entries for LRU without changing their original fixed-TTL timestamps.
behavior_after: Expiration scans the bounded registry and removes every entry older than the fixed TTL. LRU access still controls max-entry eviction but no longer changes or obstructs time-based re-fire eligibility.
tests_added: tests/python/desktop/test_watch_folder_scanner.py: reordered older entry expires while a newer entry remains suppressed.
tests/python/desktop/test_watch_folder_scanner.py: sustained newer-entry churn cannot extend a stale entry's TTL.
tests/python/desktop/test_watch_folder_scanner.py: exact TTL boundary remains inclusive and re-fire begins only after it.
tests/python/desktop/test_watch_folder_scanner.py: zero TTL never suppresses repeated detections.
manual_validation: Pre-fix focused reproduction - expected red: 2 tests failed because reordered and churn-obscured entries remained suppressed after TTL; boundary, zero-TTL, and max-entry controls passed.
